clues: As ice retreats, changing plant communities reveal stages of ecological succession.
The protected landscape offers evidence of both mountain formation and ongoing climate change.
It contains the Alps’ largest glacier within a heavily glaciated mountain area.
This World Heritage landscape lies in the Swiss Alps and was expanded beyond its original boundaries.
Look near the Jungfrau massif for the Swiss World Heritage area surrounding the largest glacier in the Alps.
targetLabel: Swiss Alps Jungfrau-Aletsch — designated property reference point
modernContext: UNESCO’s published representative point for the designated property, not its uniquely correct centre.
explanation: Glacier retreat can reveal ecological succession as well as physical changes to the mountain landscape. The combined property contains many peaks and ice bodies; its UNESCO reference point is used as a representative target, not a claim that the full mountain region has one exact centre.
dateLabel: First UNESCO World Heritage inscription year, not the age of the natural feature
cultures: Physical geography, conservation and scientific study
uncertainty: Source-checked authoring only; independent factual, English and clue-order review is pending. The point represents the designated property, not every part of a large natural feature. Source descriptions and dynamic environmental conditions may differ in date or extent; precise current measurements are not implied.
